passes.summary: This is a mature, well-instrumented Hermes installation with strong deterministic safety hooks (veto-pre-tool + hard-block/warn YAML rules), a coherent skills router architecture, and a thoughtful local-first auxiliary model fabric. The biggest real problems are reliability and token-economy footguns rather than security holes: api_max_retries:1 and mcp_discovery_timeout:0.5 make the system fragile to transient network/MCP latency (qmd has a 45s connect_timeout but discovery gives it 0.5s); prompt_caching.cache_ttl:5m and compression.target_ratio:0.2 are aggressive settings that likely lose cache hits and over-discard context in multi-agent sessions. Security posture is good (auth.json 0600, sessions 0700, redact_secrets on, comprehensive veto rules) but unsandboxed terminal + no per-session destructive-call hard enforcement verified in-hook is the main residual risk. Skills are at the edge of sprawl (ouroboros subtree dominates) and would benefit from consolidation and an explicit context-packet/swarm-consensus skill.

priority_improvements.title: api_max_retries:1 makes tasks fragile to transient network errors
priority_improvements.finding: agent.api_max_retries is set to 1. A single 429/500/connection-reset during a long 150-turn or delegated session will fail the whole task. With a multi-provider fallback chain already configured, retries are cheap insurance.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Raise to 3. Retries are orthogonal to provider fallback and prevent avoidable mid-task failures.

priority_improvements.title: mcp_discovery_timeout:0.5 can silently drop MCP servers
priority_improvements.finding: Global mcp_discovery_timeout is 0.5s. qmd itself declares connect_timeout:45 and timeout:30, signaling it is a slow-to-spawn local server (qmd-local.sh shell wrapper). A 0.5s discovery window risks the knowledge base being intermittently absent from the toolset, degrading routing/recall non-deterministically.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Raise mcp_discovery_timeout to 3-5s. The cost is a one-time startup delay; the benefit is reliable qmd availability.

priority_improvements.title: prompt_caching.cache_ttl:5m is likely a no-op or mis-set
priority_improvements.finding: Anthropic prompt caching uses fixed cache breakpoints with a 5-minute default TTL (1h available via beta header). A config value of '5m' either matches the default (no effect) or is not wired to Anthropic's extended-cache header. In long multi-agent sessions with gateway_timeout:1800 (30m), the 5m TTL guarantees cache eviction between waves of delegation, paying full input cost on each re-warm.
priority_improvements.recommendation: If Hermes supports it, set cache_ttl to 1h to retain the cached system+skills prefix across delegation waves within a 30-minute session. If the setting is not wired to the extended-cache beta, remove it to avoid false confidence and document the actual caching behavior.

priority_improvements.title: compression.target_ratio:0.2 + protect_last_n:20 over-compresses multi-agent context
priority_improvements.finding: target_ratio 0.2 compresses to 20% of original — very aggressive and prone to dropping intermediate subagent findings and tool results that the orchestrator still needs for synthesis. protect_last_n:20 is low when a fan-out wave can produce 20+ tool/result messages in a single burst, meaning genuinely recent context can be summarized away.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Loosen target_ratio to 0.3-0.35 and raise protect_last_n to 30-40 for orchestration-heavy use. Keep threshold:0.5 and protect_first_n:3. This trades modest token savings for materially better synthesis fidelity.

priority_improvements.title: Cerebras gpt-oss-120b compression with max_tokens:2048 may truncate summaries
priority_improvements.finding: auxiliary.compression uses custom:cerebras/gpt-oss-120b (fast, cheap) with max_tokens:2048 and abort_on_summary_failure:true. Cerebras is excellent for latency but an open-weight 120b summarizer at 2048 output tokens can truncate or lose nuance when compressing large 128k-context sessions, and abort_on_summary_failure means a poor/failed summary halts the session.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Keep cerebras for speed but raise compression max_tokens to ~4096, and consider a higher-quality fallback summarizer (haiku-4-5 already in the aux fleet) when the primary summary fails rather than aborting. Validate summary quality on a representative long session.

priority_improvements.title: max_turns:150 enables runaway sessions without a quality gate
priority_improvements.finding: agent.max_turns:150 is high. Combined with tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled:false, a stuck agent can burn ~150 turns and large token budgets before any hard stop. The budget hook (track-budget.py) tracks but tool_call hard_limit is 500 — both ceilings are high.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Either lower max_turns to ~80-100 for interactive sessions, or enable tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled:true so the existing hard_stop_after thresholds (exact_failure:5, idempotent_no_progress:5) actually terminate loops. The warn thresholds alone do not stop runaway loops.

priority_improvements.title: reasoning_effort:low is global; complex reasoning tasks silently degrade
priority_improvements.finding: agent.reasoning_effort:low is appropriate for the concise local-first SOUL.md profile and most tasks, but security audits, architecture decisions, and large synthesis (exactly what delegation.model:claude-opus-4-8 is escalated for) benefit from higher effort. Delegation already sets reasoning_effort:medium for children, which is good, but the top-level orchestrator stays low.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Keep global low for cost, but document/enforce that escalated work routes through delegation (medium) or explicitly raises effort. Consider a per-task override pattern in hermes-role-pipelines for high-stakes synthesis turns.

priority_improvements.title: Unsandboxed local terminal with no verified per-session destructive-call enforcement
priority_improvements.finding: terminal.backend:local runs with full user privileges; the only guardrails are veto-pre-tool.py (pattern blocks) and budget tracking. The budget policy declares destructive_calls:30 but track-budget.py is a post_tool_call hook (observes, does not pre-block); enforcement of the destructive cap as a hard stop is not evident in the pre_tool path. Veto rules are good but pattern-based and bypassable by novel command shapes (e.g., find -delete, python os.remove, truncate).
priority_improvements.recommendation: (1) Add veto hard-block patterns for find -delete, truncate -s0, python/-c os.remove/shutil.rmtree, and chmod -R on $HOME. (2) Confirm the destructive_calls:30 cap is enforced in veto-pre-tool.py (pre) not only counted in track-budget.py (post); if not, move enforcement pre-tool. (3) For untrusted/automated runs, consider terminal.backend:docker (image already configured) to sandbox.

priority_improvements.title: Browser CDP endpoint on localhost:9222 is locally reachable
priority_improvements.finding: browser.allow_private_urls:false is a good default, but cdp_url:http://localhost:9222 exposes a Chrome DevTools endpoint that any local process can drive (read cookies, navigate, exfiltrate). Combined with auto_local_for_private_urls:true, private URL fetches fall back to the local engine.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Bind CDP to a random ephemeral port with a token where supported, or ensure the browser is only launched on-demand and torn down (inactivity_timeout:120 helps). Document that any local user/process can attach to 9222 while a session is live.

priority_improvements.title: Skill sprawl: ouroboros subtree dominates and many skills are disabled, not removed
priority_improvements.finding: The autonomous-ai-agents family alone has ~30+ SKILL.md files, ~20 of them under ouroboros/* (auto, run, qa, pm, ralph, evolve, etc.). The config disabled list is very long (~90 entries) — disabling rather than consolidating keeps router/skills_hub context heavier than necessary and increases selection ambiguity.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Consolidate the ouroboros command-skills into a single ouroboros router skill with subcommands (mirroring the existing autonomous-ai-agents router pattern), reducing ~20 SKILL.md leaves to 1 router + references. Periodically prune long-disabled skills from disk rather than keeping them disabled.

priority_improvements.title: No explicit context-packet assembly skill; packet discipline lives only in prose
priority_improvements.finding: hermes-role-pipelines and hermes-agent-sync (Structured Findings Contract) are strong, but 'pass a compact context packet' is guidance, not a reusable, enforced artifact. Without a canonical packet schema, subagents are spawned with ad-hoc, often over-large context, wasting tokens at every fan-out.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Create a skill 'hermes-context-packet' defining a compact JSON packet schema (objective, scope_paths, constraints, prior_findings_refs, output_contract, budget) plus a helper to assemble it from session state. Reference it from hermes-role-pipelines as the mandatory spawn input.

priority_improvements.title: No swarm consensus/voting mechanism for conflicting subagent outputs
priority_improvements.finding: hermes-agent-sync gives deterministic file/config merge via typed findings, which handles non-conflicting changes well, but there is no mechanism for resolving contradictory conclusions from parallel agents (e.g., two reviewers disagree on a fix). The orchestrator resolves by prose synthesis, which is non-deterministic and token-heavy.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Add a lightweight consensus pattern to hermes-role-pipelines: parallel agents emit a 'verdict' finding (claim, confidence, evidence_refs); a deterministic reducer applies majority/highest-confidence-with-evidence rules, escalating ties to a single arbiter agent (opus/fable). Surface spawn-tree/HUD state to the arbiter.

priority_improvements.title: Hook timeouts (5s) are tight for memory/budget hooks under load
priority_improvements.finding: All hooks (inject-routing, capture-turn-memory, track-budget, veto-pre-tool) have timeout:5. capture-turn-memory (hindsight provider) and veto (loads YAML rule files each call) could exceed 5s under disk/CPU contention, and a veto-hook timeout that fails-open would silently disable pre-tool blocking.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Confirm veto-pre-tool.py fails CLOSED on timeout/error (block, not allow). Consider raising veto timeout to 8-10s and caching compiled rules. Memory/routing hooks failing open is acceptable; the security hook must not.

priority_improvements.title: Sessions directory not encrypted at rest
priority_improvements.finding: ~/.hermes/sessions is 0700 (good) but plaintext on disk; it can contain transcripts with secrets despite redact_secrets:true (redaction is best-effort on display, not guaranteed at storage). sessions.auto_prune:false with retention_days:90 means transcripts accumulate.
priority_improvements.recommendation: Acceptable for a single-user trusted host. If the host is shared or backed up off-box, enable filesystem-level encryption for ~/.hermes and turn on sessions.auto_prune with a shorter retention for sensitive workloads.

config_patches.rationale: Survive transient 429/5xx/connection resets during long and delegated sessions; orthogonal to provider fallback.
qmd declares connect_timeout:45; a 0.5s discovery window risks intermittently dropping the local knowledge base.
0.2 over-compresses multi-agent context; 0.33 preserves intermediate findings needed for synthesis.
A single fan-out wave can exceed 20 recent messages; protect more to avoid summarizing live context.

30-minute sessions evict a 5m cache between delegation waves; 1h (extended cache) retains the system+skills prefix. Verify the setting is wired to Anthropic's extended-cache header; if not, remove it.
Avoid truncated summaries when compressing large 128k sessions with an open-weight summarizer.
Warn-only guardrails do not stop runaway loops; enabling hard stops activates existing failure thresholds.

skill_actions.name: hermes-context-packet
skill_actions.reason: Canonical compact JSON packet schema + assembler for subagent spawning; eliminates ad-hoc oversized context and cuts fan-out token cost. Reference as mandatory input from hermes-role-pipelines.

skill_actions.name: hermes-swarm-consensus
skill_actions.reason: Deterministic verdict/confidence reducer for conflicting parallel-agent conclusions, with single-arbiter escalation (opus/fable) on ties. Complements hermes-agent-sync's non-conflicting merge.

skill_actions.name: ouroboros/* command skills
skill_actions.reason: ~20 leaf SKILL.md files (auto, run, qa, pm, ralph, evolve, status, ...) should fold into one ouroboros router skill with subcommands, mirroring the autonomous-ai-agents router; reduces skills_hub context and selection ambiguity.

skill_actions.name: hermes-role-pipelines
skill_actions.reason: Add explicit fan-out/fan-in checkpointing at subagent handoff boundaries and reference the new context-packet and swarm-consensus skills for merge/dispute handling.

skill_actions.name: all skills with external deps
skill_actions.reason: Add version pinning for external tool/runtime dependencies (uvx ouroboros-ai, firecrawl, qmd) so skill behavior is reproducible across upgrades.

security_findings.finding: Pattern-based veto can be bypassed by novel destructive shapes (find -delete, truncate -s0, python os.remove/shutil.rmtree, chmod -R $HOME).
destructive_calls:30 cap appears tracked post-hoc (track-budget.py post_tool_call) rather than enforced pre-tool. A burst of destructive calls could exceed the cap before counting catches up.
veto-pre-tool.py must fail CLOSED on timeout(5s)/error; otherwise a slow rule-load silently disables blocking.
security_findings.action: Confirm fail-closed semantics; cache compiled rules; raise veto timeout to 8-10s.

security_findings.finding: Chrome CDP on localhost:9222 is attachable by any local process (cookies/navigation/exfiltration) while a browser session is live.
security_findings.action: Use token/ephemeral-port CDP where supported; rely on inactivity_timeout teardown.

security_findings.finding: Sessions stored plaintext (0700) with auto_prune:false, 90-day retention; redact_secrets is best-effort.
security_findings.action: OK for single trusted user; enable FS encryption / shorter prune for shared or backed-up hosts.

security_findings.finding: Bitwarden secrets manager disabled; secrets live in ~/.hermes/.env (0600) which is correctly veto-blocked from writes. auth.json is 0600. This is acceptable for a single-user host.
security_findings.action: No change required; enable Bitwarden only if rotating/sharing secrets across machines.

security_findings.finding: Positives: redact_secrets:true, tirith_enabled:true, allow_private_urls:false, approvals.mode:manual, cron_mode:deny, comprehensive hard-block+warn veto rules, hooks gated by shell-hooks-allowlist with mtime pinning.
security_findings.action: Maintain; mtime-pinned hook approvals are a strong pattern.

multiagent_patterns.note: Compact packet discipline exists only as prose in hermes-role-pipelines; needs a canonical schema + assembler skill (IMP-011).
hermes-agent-sync provides typed JSON findings + apply-findings.py for deterministic, idempotent merge of non-conflicting changes. Keep and reference broadly.
No mechanism for contradictory parallel outputs; add verdict/confidence reducer with single-arbiter escalation (IMP-012).
Well covered in hermes-role-pipelines; add handoff-boundary checkpointing for resumability.

max_spawn_depth:1 (despite budget delegation_depth:4) forces parent-orchestrated waves. Skill correctly flattens trees into pipeline/supervisor shapes. Note the depth mismatch between budget policy (4) and runtime (1).
HUD (hud-active-agents.json) via track/clear-subagent-hud hooks gives visibility, but spawn-tree state is not surfaced into orchestrator context for arbitration; feed it to the consensus arbiter.
checkpoints.enabled:true exists for files but not at logical subagent handoff boundaries; add to hermes-role-pipelines for long pipelines.

config_consistency_notes: delegation.max_spawn_depth:1 contradicts budget delegation_depth:4 — align documentation so users do not plan grandchildren that cannot spawn.

Fallback ordering differs between fallback_providers (gemini-flash, cerebras, qwen3) and fallback_model (haiku, sonnet, fable). Confirm which governs which failure mode to avoid surprising cheap-model fallbacks on quality-critical tasks.
